B07C001.summary: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra did after Bhishma fell, and Sanjaya begins his account. The Kaurava army is left without a leader and falls into despair, so the kings call for Karna to take charge. Dhritarashtra doubts that Karna can fill the gap Bhishma leaves and bring his sons victory.

scenes.B07C001S01: Janamejaya asks about Dhritarashtra's grief after Bhishma's fall, and Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to report what the Kauravas did next.
scenes.B07C001S02: Sanjaya describes the Kauravas and Pandavas after Bhishma's fall and the call for Karna, and Dhritarashtra replies with doubt about whether Karna can hold the army together.

shots.B07C001S01H01: Section heading naming the Dronabhisheka Parva.
shots.B07C001S01H02: An opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati.
shots.B07C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra did after Bhishma, slain by Sikhandin, had fallen.
shots.B07C001S01H04: Vaisampayana says that Dhritarashtra, grieving, asks Sanjaya, who has come back from the camp, to report what happened.
shots.B07C001S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to tell him what the Kauravas did after Bhishma fell.
shots.B07C001S02H01: Sanjaya describes Bhishma's bed of arrows, the renewed fighting, the leaderless Kaurava army, and the kings calling for Karna.
shots.B07C001S02H02: Vaisampayana says Dhritarashtra answers Sanjaya's repeated praise of Karna with a sigh.
shots.B07C001S02H03: Dhritarashtra asks whether Karna can fill the gap left by Bhishma and fulfil his sons' hopes of victory.

B07C002.summary: Karna hears that Bhishma has fallen and hurries to the field to rescue the Kaurava army. He mourns Bhishma, declares that he will fight the Pandavas himself, and orders his armour, chariot and weapons made ready. The chapter ends with him riding out to battle in splendour.

scenes.B07C002S01: Karna goes to the field after Bhishma's fall, speaks to the soldiers, consoles the Kauravas, prepares his arms and car, and rides out to battle.

shots.B07C002S01H01: Sanjaya says Karna hurries to help the Kaurava army once he learns that Bhishma has fallen.
shots.B07C002S01H02: Karna speaks to the soldiers, mourning Bhishma's virtues and saying that without him he sees the other heroes as already lost.
shots.B07C002S01H03: Karna consoles the Kauravas, vows to slay the Pandavas, and asks for his armour, chariot and weapons to be brought.
shots.B07C002S01H04: Karna rides out to battle in a splendid chariot, and Sanjaya compares him to Indra.

B07C003.summary: Sanjaya describes Bhishma lying on his bed of arrows, the hope of the Kauravas gone. Karna dismounts in grief and approaches him on foot. He mourns the old warrior and vows to fight the Pandavas, Arjuna above all.

scenes.B07C003S01: Sanjaya describes Bhishma lying on the arrow-bed, and Karna dismounting in grief to greet him and vow to fight the Pandavas.

shots.B07C003S01H01: Sanjaya describes Bhishma lying on his arrow-bed and Karna dismounting in grief to address him, promising to avenge him against Arjuna and the Pandavas.

B07C004.summary: Bhishma, still lying on his bed of arrows, blesses Karna and tells him to lead the Kaurava army against the Pandavas. Karna takes his leave and returns to the Kaurava warriors. The Kauravas greet him with loud shouts, and Karna takes his place at the head of the army.

scenes.B07C004S01: Bhishma blesses Karna and orders him to lead the army, and Karna goes to the Kaurava warriors, who welcome him with shouts and noise.

shots.B07C004S01H01: Bhishma blesses Karna, recalls his past conquests, and orders him to lead the Kauravas in battle.
shots.B07C004S01H02: Karna takes leave of Bhishma, goes to the Kaurava warriors, and is greeted with loud shouts and noise.

B07C005.summary: Duryodhana, pleased to see Karna ready on his chariot, says the army now seems to have a proper leader. He asks Karna whom to name as commander after Bhishma, since an army cannot hold together without one. Karna answers that Drona, their teacher in arms, should lead, because the other warriors would follow him.

scenes.B07C005S01: Duryodhana asks Karna whom to appoint as commander after Bhishma, and Karna names Drona as the best choice.

shots.B07C005S01H01: Duryodhana, pleased to see Karna mounted, says the army now has a proper leader and suggests settling the matter.
shots.B07C005S01H02: Karna asks Duryodhana to speak first, since he is the wisest of the kings.
shots.B07C005S01H03: Duryodhana recalls Bhishma's leadership and asks Karna whom to appoint next, stressing that an army needs a leader.
shots.B07C005S01H04: Karna says the warriors are all worthy but Drona, their teacher and a master of arms, should be made leader.

B07C006.summary: Duryodhana turns to Drona, who is standing among the troops, and asks him to lead the army. He praises Drona's birth, learning, prowess and self-control, and compares him to the greatest gods and figures. The Kaurava kings cheer the choice, and Drona prepares to reply.

scenes.B07C006S01: Duryodhana makes his request to Drona with long praise, and the Kaurava kings cheer, and Drona prepares to answer.

shots.B07C006S01H01: Sanjaya says that Duryodhana, having heard Karna, turns to Drona in the midst of the troops.
shots.B07C006S01H02: Duryodhana praises Drona's birth, learning and skill, compares him to the greatest figures, and asks him to lead the army against the Pandavas.
shots.B07C006S01H03: The Kaurava kings cry victory to Drona and shout in approval, and Drona prepares to speak.

B07C007.summary: Drona agrees to lead, though he says he cannot kill Dhrishtadyumna, who was born to slay him. He is installed as commander with rites, and the army takes its formation, with Karna at the head of the bowmen. Both armies array for battle, omens of disaster appear, and the fighting begins with Drona driving into the Pandava ranks.

scenes.B07C007S01: Drona agrees to lead and is installed as commander, the two armies take their formations, and the battle opens with omens and Drona's assault on the Pandava ranks.

shots.B07C007S01H01: Drona says he knows the Vedas and many weapons and will fight, but he cannot slay Dhrishtadyumna, who was made for his death.
shots.B07C007S01H02: Duryodhana installs Drona as commander with proper rites, and the Kaurava army celebrates, already thinking the Pandavas beaten.
shots.B07C007S01H03: The Kaurava divisions take up their positions with Karna at the head of the bowmen, and Sanjaya describes the Pandava formation led by Arjuna and Krishna.
shots.B07C007S01H04: Sanjaya describes ill omens, the start of the battle, and Drona's fierce assault that breaks the Pandava and Panchala ranks.
shots.B07C007S01H05: Section heading marking the start of Section VIII.

B07C008.summary: Yudhishthira orders his men to surround Drona, but Drona keeps cutting down warriors across the field. Sanjaya then reports that Dhrishtadyumna has at last slain Drona, a death that brings an uproar from creatures and the gods. The Pandavas celebrate their victory with loud shouts.

scenes.B07C008S01: Yudhishthira orders the Pandavas to surround Drona, Drona's rampage through their ranks, and Sanjaya's report that Dhrishtadyumna killed him.

shots.B07C008S01H01: Sanjaya describes Yudhishthira ordering the Pandavas to surround Drona, Drona's rampage, his death at Dhrishtadyumna's hand, and the Pandavas' shouts of victory.

B07C009.summary: Dhritarashtra cannot accept that Drona, the greatest master of arms, has been killed. He asks how it happened: whether his chariot or bow broke, whether he was unarmed, and who failed to guard him. He calls the news unbearable and breaks off his questions for a while to recover himself.

scenes.B07C009S01: Dhritarashtra mourns Drona, wonders how the master could be slain, and asks Sanjaya a string of questions about the battle, then pauses his questioning.

shots.B07C009S01H01: Dhritarashtra mourns Drona, asks how he could be slain and who guarded him, and then stops to regain his senses before asking more.

B07C010.summary: Dhritarashtra faints on hearing of Drona's death, and his attendants and the royal ladies revive him. Once he regains his senses, he asks Sanjaya to describe the battle again. He then asks, hero by hero, which Kaurava warriors stood against each Pandava ally rushing at Drona, and he ends by calling on Krishna to restore his firmness.

scenes.B07C010S01: Dhritarashtra faints, is revived by his attendants, and asks Sanjaya a long series of questions about which Kaurava warriors opposed each Pandava hero as they attacked Drona.

shots.B07C010S01H01: Vaisampayana says Dhritarashtra, overcome by grief, faints, is revived by his attendants and the royal women, and then asks Sanjaya to tell him about the battle.
shots.B07C010S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks, one by one, who in his army resisted each Pandava and their allies as they rushed at Drona, and then calls on Krishna to steady him.

B07C011.summary: Dhritarashtra recounts Krishna's feats from boyhood onward, including his victories over demons and kings, and concludes that the Kurus cannot win if Krishna and Arjuna fight together. He blames himself for the ruin of his family, now that Bhishma and Drona are dead. He asks Sanjaya to tell him everything about the battle.

scenes.B07C011S01: Dhritarashtra praises Krishna's exploits, predicts Kaurava defeat if Krishna joins the Pandavas, blames his own acts for the ruin, and asks for a full account of the battle.

shots.B07C011S01H01: Dhritarashtra recounts Krishna's feats since boyhood, the allies who will join the Pandavas, and his own guilt for the Kurus' ruin, and asks Sanjaya to describe the battle.

B07C012.summary: Sanjaya begins the account of Drona's fall. Once made commander, Drona offers Duryodhana a boon, and Duryodhana asks him to take Yudhishthira alive. Drona is puzzled, but agrees on the condition that Arjuna is drawn away from the field, and Duryodhana then proclaims the promise to the whole army.

scenes.B07C012S01: Drona offers a boon, Duryodhana asks for Yudhishthira to be seized alive, Drona agrees on conditions, and Duryodhana publicizes the pledge.

shots.B07C012S01H01: Sanjaya says he will describe Drona's fall, then reports Drona's offer of a boon, Duryodhana's request for Yudhishthira to be taken alive, and Drona's guarded reply.
shots.B07C012S01H02: Drona explains that Arjuna, his pupil, is too strong to oppose, so Arjuna must be drawn away before Yudhishthira can be seized.
shots.B07C012S01H03: Sanjaya says Duryodhana made Drona's promise known to all the troops, and that the sons regarded Yudhishthira as already taken.

B07C013.summary: Yudhishthira learns through spies of Drona's pledge to take him, and he asks Arjuna to stay close and protect him. Arjuna vows that Yudhishthira will not be taken, though he will not harm his teacher, and says he has never broken a promise. The two armies join battle, and Drona breaks through the Pandava ranks toward Dhrishtadyumna's division.

scenes.B07C013S01: Yudhishthira hears of Drona's pledge and asks Arjuna to protect him, Arjuna vows to do so, and the armies clash while Drona attacks Dhrishtadyumna's division.

shots.B07C013S01H01: Sanjaya reports the Kaurava shouts over the pledge, and Yudhishthira learning of it through spies and asking Arjuna to fight close by.
shots.B07C013S01H02: Arjuna vows to keep Yudhishthira from capture, though he will not kill his teacher, and says he has never broken a vow.
shots.B07C013S01H03: Sanjaya describes the battle beginning, the two sides held in a deadlock by Drona and Arjuna, and Drona then driving into Dhrishtadyumna's division.

B07C014.summary: Drona tears through the Pandava ranks with such fury that Sanjaya compares the carnage to a vast river of blood and corpses. The Pandava champions then rush at him, and many single combats break out across the field. Abhimanyu duels with Paurava, Jayadratha and Salya, and after he hurls back Salya's dart, the Kauravas surround him.

scenes.B07C014S01: Drona's rampage is described as a river of carnage, the Pandava champions attack him, and a series of single combats ends with the Kauravas closing in on Abhimanyu.

shots.B07C014S01H01: Sanjaya describes Drona's assault as a terrible river of blood and dead, with the fallen warriors and their weapons making up its parts.
shots.B07C014S01H02: Many single combats follow, including Sakuni and Sahadeva, Bhima and Vivinsati, Nakula and Salya, and Abhimanyu's duels with Paurava, Jayadratha and Salya, before the Kauravas surround Abhimanyu.

B07C015.summary: Dhritarashtra admits he envies those who can see such fights, but says he is not satisfied by the account and asks about Salya's combat with Abhimanyu. Sanjaya reports that Bhima, not Abhimanyu, takes up the fight with Salya, and the two strike each other with maces until both fall. Kritavarman carries Salya from the field, and the Kaurava army flees before the Pandavas.

scenes.B07C015S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Salya's combat with Abhimanyu, Sanjaya describes Salya and Bhima's mace duel, and the Kaurava army breaks and flees.

shots.B07C015S01H01: Dhritarashtra says he envies those who can see such duels, and asks Sanjaya to tell him about Salya and Abhimanyu.
shots.B07C015S01H02: Sanjaya describes Salya and Bhima's mace duel, in which both fall, Kritavarman carries Salya away, and the Pandavas drive the Kaurava army in flight.

B07C016.summary: Vrishasena, son of Karna, holds back the Pandava attack single-handed, until the Pandava princes and then Drona's son and others join the fight. Drona then charges Yudhishthira and kills his protectors, while the Pandava warriors cry out that the king is slain. Arjuna arrives with a devastating rush, and as darkness falls both sides withdraw from the field.

scenes.B07C016S01: Vrishasena fights off the Pandava warriors, Drona charges Yudhishthira and kills his defenders, Arjuna arrives, and the two sides break off at sunset.

shots.B07C016S01H01: Sanjaya describes Vrishasena's lone stand, Drona's charge at Yudhishthira, Arjuna's arrival, and the withdrawal of both sides as the sun sets.

B07C017.summary: Drona tells Duryodhana that Arjuna must be lured away from Yudhishthira before Yudhishthira can be seized. The Trigarta brothers and their allies swear a fire-oath to draw Arjuna off and kill him or die trying, and Arjuna accepts their challenge. Yudhishthira blesses him and names Satyajit as his protector, and Arjuna rides out against the Trigartas, leaving both armies to clash.

scenes.B07C017S01: Drona asks Duryodhana to lure Arjuna away, the Trigartas swear an oath to do so, Arjuna takes up the challenge with Yudhishthira's leave, and the armies clash.

shots.B07C017S01H01: Drona tells Duryodhana that Arjuna must be drawn away before Yudhishthira can be seized, and that he will then take Yudhishthira himself.
shots.B07C017S01H02: The Trigarta ruler and his brothers vow to draw Arjuna away and kill him, and their allies swear the same oath by fire, and Arjuna accepts their challenge.
shots.B07C017S01H03: Yudhishthira warns Arjuna that Drona has resolved to seize him and asks Arjuna to thwart the plan.
shots.B07C017S01H04: Arjuna names Satyajit as Yudhishthira's protector, and says that if Satyajit falls Yudhishthira should leave the field.
shots.B07C017S01H05: Yudhishthira blesses Arjuna, who rides out against the Trigartas, and the two armies clash with great force.

B07C018.summary: The Samsaptakas, the band of warriors sworn to kill Arjuna, form up in a half-moon and meet him in the field. Arjuna blows his conch, and the enemy is stunned with fear, but they recover and pour arrows on him. After he kills Sudhanwan, his followers flee, until the Trigarta king rallies them and they return to face Arjuna.

scenes.B07C018S01: The Samsaptakas meet Arjuna in battle, he stuns them with his conch and kills Sudhanwan, and their king rallies the fleeing warriors to return to the fight.

shots.B07C018S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Samsaptakas' half-moon formation, Arjuna's conch blast that stuns them, his killing of Sudhanwan, and the Trigarta king rallying the fleeing warriors.

B07C019.summary: Arjuna drives back into the Samsaptakas with Krishna at the reins. They bury him and Krishna in arrows, so he uses a weapon that creates thousands of images of himself and Krishna, and the troops in confusion kill each other. Krishna, worn out, calls to Arjuna, who then clears the sky with a wind weapon and slaughters the Samsaptakas. While this goes on, Drona attacks Yudhishthira.

scenes.B07C019S01: Arjuna and Krishna fight the Samsaptakas, using illusory weapons and a wind weapon to win, while Drona presses his assault on Yudhishthira.

shots.B07C019S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's charge against the Samsaptakas, the illusory images that confuse the enemy, Krishna's worry, the wind weapon, the slaughter that follows, and Drona's attack on Yudhishthira.

B07C020.summary: After Arjuna has gone off after the Samsaptakas, Drona forms the Kaurava army in the shape of a Garuda and marches to seize Yudhishthira. Yudhishthira answers with a counter-formation and asks Dhrishtadyumna to keep Drona from him. Dhrishtadyumna vows to hold Drona back, but Durmukha engages him, and the battle becomes a chaotic slaughter of men and elephants as Drona presses on toward Yudhishthira.

scenes.B07C020S01: Drona arrays the Kaurava army as a Garuda, Yudhishthira prepares a counter-array and asks Dhrishtadyumna for protection, and the battle degenerates into a bloody melee that carries Drona toward Yudhishthira.

shots.B07C020S01H01: Drona arrays the Kaurava army in the shape of a Garuda with himself in its mouth, and Yudhishthira answers with a counter-array and asks Dhrishtadyumna to keep Drona from taking him.
shots.B07C020S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna vows that Drona will never seize Yudhishthira while he lives.
shots.B07C020S01H03: Dhrishtadyumna charges Drona, Durmukha blocks him, and the battle becomes a chaotic slaughter of men and elephants that ends with Drona pressing toward Yudhishthira.

B07C021.summary: Satyajit, the Panchala prince, fights Drona fiercely, but Drona destroys his bows, horses and charioteer and at last beheads him. Yudhishthira flees, and Satanika, a Matsya prince, is also beheaded by Drona. Drona then sweeps through the Pandava ranks, and many Pandava warriors close in on him in turn, all falling before him as Drona routs the Panchalas and Matsyas.

scenes.B07C021S01: Drona kills Satyajit and Satanika, Yudhishthira flees, and a rush of Pandava warriors fails to stop Drona as he routs their armies.

shots.B07C021S01H01: Sanjaya describes Satyajit's duel with Drona, which ends with Satyajit beheaded, then Yudhishthira's flight, Satanika's death, and Drona's rampage through the Pandava ranks.
shots.B07C021S01H02: Many Pandava warriors attack Drona and fall one after another, Yudhishthira flees again, and Drona routs the Panchalas and Matsyas.

B07C022.summary: Dhritarashtra asks whether anyone dared to stand against Drona once the Pandavas were broken. Sanjaya reports that the Kauravas pressed their advantage, and Duryodhana gloated to Karna that the enemy was finished. Karna warns that the Pandavas will not give up, and that Bhima and the others are returning to surround Drona. Duryodhana then rides to Drona's car, and the Pandava warriors come back, all bent on killing him.

scenes.B07C022S01: Dhritarashtra asks who stood against Drona, Duryodhana boasts to Karna of the enemy's defeat, Karna warns of the Pandava return, and both sides move back toward Drona.

shots.B07C022S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks whether anyone dared to face Drona after the Pandavas were broken, praising Drona's fearless resolve.
shots.B07C022S01H02: Sanjaya says the Kauravas, seeing the enemy routed, assailed their fleeing forces from all sides, and Duryodhana laughed as he spoke to Karna.
shots.B07C022S01H03: Duryodhana boasts that the Panchalas are broken, that Bhima stands alone among his foes, and that the Pandavas have lost hope.
shots.B07C022S01H04: Karna replies that the Pandavas will not flee, recalls their grievances, and warns that Bhima and the others are coming to surround Drona.
shots.B07C022S01H05: Duryodhana rides to Drona's car with his brothers, while the Pandava warriors return to the fight, all determined to kill Drona.

B07C023.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name the warriors who rushed at Drona under Bhima, and by what marks they are known. Sanjaya gives a long roll-call of the Pandava allies, their horses, standards and bows, and describes the great host that advanced. He then reports the many single combats that broke out across the field, a battle that Sanjaya says had never been seen before.

scenes.B07C023S01: Dhritarashtra asks for the warriors who attacked Drona, Sanjaya lists them by their horses, standards and bows, and then describes the many duels that broke out across the field.

shots.B07C023S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe the distinguishing marks of the chariots of the warriors who attacked Drona under Bhima.
shots.B07C023S01H02: Sanjaya lists the Pandava allies advancing on Drona, each identified by the colour and breed of his horses, from Satyaki and Yudhishthira to the Panchala princes and their followers.
shots.B07C023S01H03: Sanjaya describes the standards and bows of the Pandava warriors, such as Bhima's silver lion and Yudhishthira's golden moon, and says the host looked like painted images.
shots.B07C023S01H04: Sanjaya reports many single combats across the field, including Drupada against Drona, Virata against Vinda and Anuvinda, and Ghatotkacha against Alambusha, with battle breaking out everywhere.
shots.B07C023S01H05: Section heading marking the start of Section XXIV.

B07C024.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Arjuna fought the Samsaptakas and what the Kaurava warriors did in the meantime. Sanjaya describes Bhima routing Duryodhana's elephant division and killing the Anga king. Bhima then faces Bhagadatta's elephant Supratika, escapes it by getting under its belly, and the rumour spreads that he is dead. Bhagadatta's elephant then rampages through the Pandava ranks.

scenes.B07C024S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Arjuna, Sanjaya describes Bhima's fight with Duryodhana's elephants and Bhagadatta's elephant, and Bhagadatta's elephant rampages through the Pandava host.

shots.B07C024S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Arjuna fought, what he did to the Samsaptakas, and what the Samsaptakas did to him.
shots.B07C024S01H02: Bhima routs Duryodhana's elephant division, cuts Duryodhana's bow and standard, and kills the Anga king on his elephant, and the Kaurava division flees.
shots.B07C024S01H03: Bhagadatta's elephant Supratika fights Bhima, who escapes by getting under its belly; the Pandavas hear a false cry that Bhima is dead, and Bhagadatta's elephant then routs them, killing Ruchiparvan and driving off Yuyutsu.

B07C025.summary: Sanjaya turns to Arjuna's deeds. Seeing Bhagadatta's rampage, Arjuna asks Krishna to drive toward him, but the Samsaptakas return to challenge Arjuna, and he is torn between the two. He decides to destroy the Samsaptakas first, which is what Duryodhana and Karna had hoped for, and he wipes them out with the Brahma weapon. Krishna praises him, and Arjuna then tells Krishna to go on to Bhagadatta.

scenes.B07C025S01: Arjuna sets out for Bhagadatta, is challenged by the Samsaptakas, chooses to destroy them first with the Brahma weapon, earns Krishna's praise, and turns to Bhagadatta.

shots.B07C025S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's dilemma between Bhagadatta and the Samsaptakas, his slaughter of the Samsaptakas with the Brahma weapon, and Krishna's praise before Arjuna orders the advance on Bhagadatta.

B07C026.summary: Arjuna turns aside to fight Susharman, defeats him and his brothers, and then sweeps through the Kaurava host. He meets Bhagadatta on his elephant, and Krishna steers the car so that the elephant is on his left. Arjuna holds back from striking the rider from behind, keeping to the rules of fair fight, while the elephant kills many other warriors.

scenes.B07C026S01: Arjuna defeats Susharman and his brothers, scatters the Kaurava host, and sets up a clash with Bhagadatta's elephant, where he refuses to strike from behind.

shots.B07C026S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's turn against Susharman and his brothers, his sweep through the Kaurava host, and his clash with Bhagadatta, whom he refuses to strike from behind.

B07C027.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Arjuna and Bhagadatta fought to the end. Sanjaya describes Arjuna cutting down Bhagadatta's weapons and armour and striking the elephant. When Bhagadatta's Vaishnava weapon lands on Krishna's chest and turns into a garland, Arjuna complains that Krishna had promised only to drive. Krishna explains the weapon's history and why he let it strike, and Arjuna then kills the elephant and Bhagadatta, whose death breaks the Kaurava warriors.

scenes.B07C027S01: Dhritarashtra asks how the duel ended, Sanjaya describes the fight between Arjuna and Bhagadatta, and Krishna explains the Vaishnava weapon before Arjuna kills Bhagadatta.

shots.B07C027S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what Arjuna did to Bhagadatta and what Bhagadatta did to Arjuna.
shots.B07C027S01H02: Sanjaya describes Arjuna cutting down Bhagadatta's weapons, armour and elephant, Bhagadatta's Vaishnava weapon turning into a garland on Krishna's chest, Krishna's account of its history, and Arjuna's killing of Bhagadatta.

B07C028.summary: After killing Bhagadatta, Arjuna fights the Gandhara brothers Vrishaka and Achala, Sakuni's brothers, and kills them with a single arrow. Sakuni then conjures illusions against Arjuna, which Arjuna destroys one by one until Sakuni flees. Arjuna's arrows split the Kaurava host, and the field becomes a scene of carnage in which men abandon their own kin in panic.

scenes.B07C028S01: Arjuna kills Vrishaka and Achala, Sakuni conjures illusions that Arjuna dispels, Sakuni flees, and Arjuna's arrows cut down the Kaurava host.

shots.B07C028S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna circling Bhagadatta's body and killing Vrishaka and Achala with a single arrow after they attack him from both sides.
shots.B07C028S01H02: Sakuni's illusions are destroyed by Arjuna, Sakuni flees, Arjuna's arrows split the Kaurava army, and the battlefield is left in panic and carnage.

B07C029.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how his men felt after the rout and how they rallied. Sanjaya says that the Kuru champions still followed Drona and seized an opening against Bhima's side, while the two armies fought furiously over Drona's life. Dhrishtadyumna finally checks Drona. Nila then attacks the Kaurava ranks, but Drona's son Ashvatthama kills him, and the Pandavas fear that Arjuna is too far away to help.

scenes.B07C029S01: Dhritarashtra asks about the Kaurava mood after the rout, Sanjaya describes the fierce struggle over Drona, and Ashvatthama kills Nila while the Pandavas lose heart.

shots.B07C029S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what the Kauravas felt when their divisions were routed and how they could rally from such flight.
shots.B07C029S01H02: Sanjaya describes the Kurus seizing an opening against Bhima's side, the two armies fighting over Drona's life, and Dhrishtadyumna finally checking Drona.
shots.B07C029S01H03: Nila attacks the Kaurava ranks, but Ashvatthama kills him, and the Pandavas fear that Arjuna is too far away to rescue them.

B07C030.summary: Bhima, unable to bear the slaughter of his army, attacks Valhika and Karna, and Drona wounds him in return. The Pandavas gather around Bhima and press in on Drona's car, while Arjuna, having destroyed the Samsaptakas, storms in and scorches the Kauravas. Karna meets Arjuna with the fire weapon, and when Satyaki and others attack him, Duryodhana and Drona rescue him. At sunset both armies withdraw, bloodied and worn.

scenes.B07C030S01: Bhima, Drona and the Pandava host clash in a furious melee, Arjuna arrives and fights Karna, Karna is rescued from Satyaki, and both armies withdraw at sunset.

shots.B07C030S01H01: Sanjaya describes the long battle around Drona's car, from Bhima's attacks and the Pandava rally through Arjuna's arrival, his clash with Karna, and the withdrawal of both armies at sunset.

B07C031.summary: The Kauravas retire humiliated, and Duryodhana rebukes Drona for letting Yudhishthira escape. Drona promises to form an impenetrable circular array and asks that Arjuna be drawn away, and the Samsaptakas lure him off. Abhimanyu breaks into the array, but he is overwhelmed by six warriors and finally killed by Duhsasana's son. Dhritarashtra grieves for the boy and asks how so many warriors could kill him.

scenes.B07C031S01: The Kauravas retire after defeat, Duryodhana blames Drona, Drona sets up his array while the Samsaptakas draw Arjuna away, Abhimanyu breaks in and falls, and Dhritarashtra laments.
scenes.B07C031S02: Sanjaya agrees to describe the slaying of Abhimanyu in detail.

shots.B07C031S01H01: Heading naming the Abhimanyu-badha Parva, the section on the slaying of Abhimanyu.
shots.B07C031S01H02: Sanjaya says the Kauravas, beaten by Arjuna and disheartened, retire from the field with Drona's consent and pass a silent, cursed night.
shots.B07C031S01H03: Duryodhana rebukes Drona for failing to seize Yudhishthira, and Drona answers by promising to kill a great Pandava warrior and form an impenetrable array, if Arjuna can be drawn away.
shots.B07C031S01H04: The Samsaptakas challenge Arjuna again, Drona forms his circular array, and Abhimanyu, ordered by Yudhishthira, breaks into it before six warriors and Duhsasana's son kill him.
shots.B07C031S01H05: Dhritarashtra grieves that a boy was slain by so many grown warriors and asks Sanjaya to tell how it happened.
shots.B07C031S02H01: Sanjaya says he will describe in detail how Abhimanyu broke into the Kaurava ranks and how the warriors were struck down.

B07C032.summary: Sanjaya lavishes praise on the Pandavas, Krishna and especially on Abhimanyu, who seemed to combine the best qualities of them all. Dhritarashtra asks for a detailed account of the boy's death, and Sanjaya asks him to bear his grief. He then describes the great circular array Drona formed, with Duryodhana in its midst, Lakshmana leading ten thousand warriors and Jayadratha, Sakuni and Salya on its flanks, and the battle begins.

scenes.B07C032S01: Sanjaya praises the Pandavas and Abhimanyu, Dhritarashtra asks for an account of his death, and Sanjaya describes the Kaurava circular array before the battle begins.

shots.B07C032S01H01: Sanjaya praises the Pandavas, Krishna and Yudhishthira, and says Abhimanyu had the qualities of all of them.
shots.B07C032S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to tell him in detail how the invincible Abhimanyu was slain.
shots.B07C032S01H03: Sanjaya tells the king to be still and bear his grief, and promises to describe the great slaughter of his kinsmen.
shots.B07C032S01H04: Sanjaya describes Drona's circular array, with the kings and princes at its heads and Duryodhana in its midst, and the armies begin to fight to the death.

B07C033.summary: The Pandava host, led by Bhima, attacks Drona's array, but Drona holds them back with a storm of arrows. Yudhishthira, unable to break the array, asks Abhimanyu to break in and open a passage, and Abhimanyu accepts, promising that the others will follow. Yudhishthira blesses him, and Abhimanyu orders his charioteer to drive into Drona's army.

scenes.B07C033S01: The Pandavas fail to break Drona's array, Yudhishthira asks Abhimanyu to do it, and Abhimanyu and the Pandava leaders agree.
scenes.B07C033S02: Yudhishthira blesses Abhimanyu, and Abhimanyu orders his charioteer to drive toward Drona's army.

shots.B07C033S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Pandava leaders attacking Drona's array, Drona driving them back, and Yudhishthira deciding to send Abhimanyu in to break it.
shots.B07C033S01H02: Abhimanyu says he has been taught how to break such an array, but he may not be able to come back out if he is trapped.
shots.B07C033S01H03: Yudhishthira tells Abhimanyu to break the array once so the Pandavas can follow him through.
shots.B07C033S01H04: Bhima promises to follow Abhimanyu with Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki and the others, and to enter the array again and again.
shots.B07C033S01H05: Abhimanyu vows to penetrate Drona's array and to slaughter the enemy single-handed, or not count himself Arjuna's son.
shots.B07C033S02H01: Yudhishthira blesses Abhimanyu and asks that his strength be increased.
shots.B07C033S02H02: Sanjaya says Abhimanyu orders his charioteer Sumitra to drive quickly toward Drona's army.

B07C034.summary: Sumitra, Abhimanyu's charioteer, warns him that Drona is a master of arms and that Abhimanyu, pampered by luxury, is untested in battle. Abhimanyu laughs off the warning and drives on, breaking into the circular array while the Kauravas close in. He kills warrior after warrior, along with their elephants, steeds and cars, until the Kaurava army loses heart and flees, abandoning its wounded.

scenes.B07C034S01: Sumitra warns Abhimanyu against recklessness, Abhimanyu drives into Drona's array, and he cuts down warriors and beasts until the Kauravas flee in terror.

shots.B07C034S01H01: Sumitra warns Abhimanyu that Drona is a master of arms and that Abhimanyu, raised in luxury, is untested, but Abhimanyu urges him forward.
shots.B07C034S01H02: Abhimanyu boasts that he fears no one, breaks into Drona's array, and slaughters warriors, elephants and steeds, until the Kauravas lose heart and flee, leaving their wounded kin on the field.

B07C035.summary: Duryodhana, enraged by the rout, turns on Abhimanyu, and Drona orders his warriors to rescue the king. Drona, Karna, Kripa, Salya and many others close in on Abhimanyu, who fights them all off. He kills the ruler of the Asmakas, wounds Karna, and drives Salya from his chariot in a faint, and then the Kaurava army runs. The gods and other beings praise him for his prowess.

scenes.B07C035S01: Duryodhana attacks Abhimanyu, Drona orders the king rescued, the Kaurava warriors surround Abhimanyu, and he kills and wounds his way through them until the army flees.

shots.B07C035S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava warriors surrounding Abhimanyu, his wounding of Karna and Salya, his killing of the Asmaka ruler, and the rout that follows, with the gods praising him.

B07C036.summary: Dhritarashtra asks which warriors tried to check Abhimanyu as he broke the Kaurava chariot ranks, and Sanjaya begins with Abhimanyu's exploits. Salya's younger brother rushes at him and is killed with his charioteer and car. His followers come next, and Abhimanyu fights them first gently and then with great ferocity, until the Kaurava chariots turn and flee.

scenes.B07C036S01: Dhritarashtra asks who opposed Abhimanyu, Sanjaya describes Salya's brother's death, and Abhimanyu routs the followers who come after him.

shots.B07C036S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks which warriors of his army tried to check Abhimanyu while he was grinding down the foremost bowmen.
shots.B07C036S01H02: Sanjaya says he will describe Abhimanyu's prowess as he broke the chariot ranks, protected by Drona himself.
shots.B07C036S01H03: Salya's younger brother attacks Abhimanyu and is killed, with his charioteer, car and all his gear, and the onlookers cheer.
shots.B07C036S01H04: The followers of Salya's brother rush at Abhimanyu, who fights them first gently and then fiercely until the Kaurava car-division turns and flees.

B07C037.summary: Dhritarashtra, torn between shame and pride at his son's army being held off by one youth, asks Sanjaya for the full story again. Sanjaya tells how Abhimanyu strikes down many of the Kaurava chiefs. Drona praises Abhimanyu to Kripa, and Duryodhana sneers that Drona is shielding his pupil's son, then orders an attack. Duhsasana vows to kill Abhimanyu himself and goes in against him.

scenes.B07C037S01: Dhritarashtra asks for the story again, Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu's rampage and Drona's praise, Duryodhana orders the attack, and Duhsasana fights Abhimanyu in a car duel.

shots.B07C037S01H01: Dhritarashtra says he feels both shame and pride that one youth held off his son's army, and asks for the whole account of the encounter again.
shots.B07C037S01H02: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu's rampage through the Kaurava chiefs, Drona's praise of him to Kripa, Duryodhana's sneer, the order to attack, and Duhsasana's car duel with Abhimanyu.

B07C038.summary: Abhimanyu taunts Duhsasana for his harsh speech, his part in the dice game, and his cruelty, and he swears to repay the wrongs done to his family. He wounds Duhsasana, who faints and is carried away, and the Pandavas cheer. Karna then comes forward and rains arrows on Abhimanyu, but Abhimanyu brings down his umbrella, standard, charioteer and steeds, and then breaks his bow.

scenes.B07C038S01: Abhimanyu taunts and wounds Duhsasana, who is carried off, Karna challenges Abhimanyu and is stripped of his umbrella, steeds and bow, and the Pandavas rejoice.

shots.B07C038S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu taunting Duhsasana, wounding him so he falls into a swoon and is carried off, Karna's counterattack, and Abhimanyu breaking Karna's bow and standard.

B07C039.summary: Karna's younger brother rushes in and is slain by Abhimanyu with a single arrow. Karna, shaken, flees the field, and Abhimanyu sweeps through the Kaurava army, leaving only Jayadratha standing in the midst of it. The field becomes impassable with bodies, and Sanjaya says Abhimanyu blazed like the noonday sun among the enemy.

scenes.B07C039S01: Karna's brother is killed, Karna flees, Abhimanyu routs the Kaurava army, and the field is strewn with the dead as Abhimanyu blazes through the enemy.

shots.B07C039S01H01: Sanjaya describes Karna's brother slain, Karna's flight, the rout of the Kaurava army, and Abhimanyu blazing through the field until the dead make it impassable.

B07C040.summary: Dhritarashtra asks whether any great Pandava warriors followed Abhimanyu into the Kaurava host. Sanjaya says Yudhishthira, Bhima and the other leaders rushed in, but Jayadratha rallied the fleeing Kauravas and held the Pandavas back. Dhritarashtra asks what made Jayadratha so strong, and Sanjaya tells how, after Bhima humbled him for insulting Draupadi, he won a boon from Mahadeva (Shiva) that let him hold off the Pandavas.

scenes.B07C040S01: Dhritarashtra asks about the Pandava pursuit, Sanjaya says Jayadratha rallied the Kauravas, and Sanjaya explains Jayadratha's austerities and the boon he received from Mahadeva.

shots.B07C040S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks whether any great warrior in Yudhishthira's army followed Abhimanyu into the Kaurava ranks.
shots.B07C040S01H02: Sanjaya says the Pandava leaders rushed after Abhimanyu, but Jayadratha rallied the fleeing Kauravas and checked the Pandavas.
shots.B07C040S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks what austerities and gifts gave Jayadratha the strength to hold off the Pandavas alone.
shots.B07C040S01H04: Sanjaya tells how Jayadratha, humbled by Bhima, performed severe austerities, won Mahadeva's boon to check the four other Pandavas, and then held the Pandava host on his own.

B07C041.summary: Sanjaya describes Jayadratha's splendid chariot and his attacks on Satyaki, Bhima, Drupada, Yudhishthira and the other Pandava leaders. Yudhishthira cuts his bow, but Jayadratha quickly takes another and fells Bhima's bow and standard, forcing Bhima to leap onto Satyaki's car. No Pandava can get past him, and he closes the gap Abhimanyu had opened, thanks to Mahadeva's boon.

scenes.B07C041S01: Jayadratha, on his magnificent chariot, fights off the Pandava leaders one after another and closes the path Abhimanyu had opened.

shots.B07C041S01H01: Sanjaya describes Jayadratha's splendid chariot, his attacks on the Pandava leaders, the exchange in which Yudhishthira's arrow cuts his bow, and his blocking of every Pandava attempt to pass, thanks to the boon.

B07C042.summary: Abhimanyu cuts into the Kaurava ranks, disabling Vrishasena's chariot and killing the warrior Vasatiya. Many Kshatriyas then surround him, but he cuts down their bows, arms and heads until the field is strewn with bodies. He moves so fast that he seems almost invisible, blazing like the sun among the enemy.

scenes.B07C042S01: Abhimanyu drives Vrishasena from the field, kills Vasatiya, and slaughters the warriors who surround him until the battlefield is strewn with dead.

shots.B07C042S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu disabling Vrishasena's chariot, killing Vasatiya, and then cutting down the warriors who surround him until the field is covered with dead and he seems to vanish in the dust.

B07C043.summary: Abhimanyu seizes Satyasravas, and a crowd of warriors rushes at him. Rukmaratha, the son of Salya, vows to take him alive, but he is slain, and Salya's princely kin come forward to fight. Abhimanyu uses the Gandharva weapon to create many illusory forms and kills a hundred princes. Duryodhana, alarmed by the slaughter, goes after him, and Abhimanyu's arrows force him to turn back.

scenes.B07C043S01: Abhimanyu seizes Satyasravas, slays Rukmaratha and a band of princes with the Gandharva weapon, and drives Duryodhana back.

shots.B07C043S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu seizing Satyasravas, Rukmaratha's death, the Gandharva illusions that let him slay a hundred princes, and Duryodhana being driven back.

B07C044.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what his army did next, after Duryodhana was beaten back and a hundred princes slain. Sanjaya says the Kaurava troops fled in despair until Drona, Kripa, Karna and others attacked Abhimanyu. Lakshmana, Duryodhana's son, rushed in alone, and Abhimanyu killed him with one arrow after taunting Duryodhana. Duryodhana's fury brings six great warriors against Abhimanyu, and he breaks through an elephant division and kills Kratha's son before the Kauravas retreat.

scenes.B07C044S01: The Kaurava army flees, Drona and others attack Abhimanyu, Lakshmana is slain, and Abhimanyu breaks through the elephant division and kills Kratha's son.

shots.B07C044S01H01: Dhritarashtra calls Abhimanyu's prowess almost incredible and asks what his army did next after Duryodhana was beaten back and a hundred princes slain.
shots.B07C044S01H02: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava flight, the attack by Drona and his allies, Abhimanyu's killing of Lakshmana, the six warriors who surround him, and his killing of Kratha's son, after which the Kauravas turn away.

B07C045.summary: Dhritarashtra asks which of his warriors surrounded Abhimanyu as he rode through the army on his fleet steeds. Sanjaya says the kings fled before him, and Drona, Kripa, Karna, Ashvatthama and others attacked him, but he held them off and shot down their steeds, charioteers and bows. He killed Vrindaraka, wounded Ashvatthama and Karna, and then killed the ruler of the Kosalas, whose death sent ten thousand kings fleeing.

scenes.B07C045S01: Dhritarashtra asks who surrounded Abhimanyu, Sanjaya describes the six great warriors' attacks, and Abhimanyu's killings and wounds scatter the Kaurava kings.

shots.B07C045S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks which warriors of his army surrounded Abhimanyu while he rode his three-year-old steeds through the field.
shots.B07C045S01H02: Sanjaya describes the kings fleeing, the six great warriors attacking Abhimanyu, his shots at Drona, Kripa, Karna and Ashvatthama, his killing of Vrindaraka, and his slaying of the ruler of the Kosalas, which sends ten thousand kings in flight.

B07C046.summary: Karna and Abhimanyu trade arrows until both are drenched in blood, and Abhimanyu kills many more warriors, including Karna's counsellors and several princes. Drona then advises the Kauravas to disarm Abhimanyu rather than fight him head on, and Karna, Kritavarman and Kripa cut his bow, steeds and charioteers. Abhimanyu leaps into the air with sword and shield, but Drona and Karna cut those away too. He comes down and charges Drona with a car-wheel in his hands.

scenes.B07C046S01: Abhimanyu duels Karna and kills many warriors, Drona advises disarming him, the Kauravas strip him of his bow, steeds and charioteers, and he is left to charge Drona with a wheel.

shots.B07C046S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu's duel with Karna, his killing of many warriors, Drona's advice to disarm him, the Kaurava warriors cutting away his bow, steeds and charioteers, and Abhimanyu, stripped of sword and shield, charging Drona with a wheel.
shots.B07C046S01H02: Section heading marking the start of Section XLVII.

B07C047.summary: Abhimanyu, stripped of his bow, sword and wheel, takes up a mace and fights Ashvatthama, Kalikeya and Duhsasana's son, but Duhsasana's son strikes him on the head as he rises, and he falls dead. The Kauravas rejoice, though voices in the sky call the killing unrighteous. Yudhishthira rallies his routed troops, telling them the boy has gone to the regions of the righteous.

scenes.B07C047S01: Abhimanyu is disarmed, fights on with a mace, and is killed by Duhsasana's son, and Yudhishthira then rallies his routed troops.

shots.B07C047S01H01: Sanjaya describes Abhimanyu's wheel being shattered, his mace fight with Ashvatthama, Kalikeya and Duhsasana's son, and his death from a blow to the head, while the Kauravas rejoice.
shots.B07C047S01H02: Sanjaya says the Pandava troops break, and Yudhishthira rallies them by saying the boy has gone to heaven and that they will still win.

B07C048.summary: Sanjaya says the Kaurava army returns to camp in the evening, bloodied and shaken. At dusk the field is left to carrion eaters and Rakshasas, and a river of blood runs through the heaps of corpses. The warriors leave Abhimanyu lying among the dead, like a sacrificial fire no longer fed with butter.

scenes.B07C048S01: The Kauravas leave the field at dusk, and Sanjaya describes the battlefield of corpses, the scavengers, the river of blood, and Abhimanyu's body.

shots.B07C048S01H01: Sanjaya describes the evening withdrawal, the field strewn with dead animals and men, the scavengers and Rakshasas feasting, the river of blood, and Abhimanyu lying like a fire no longer fed with butter.

B07C049.summary: The Pandava warriors lay down their arms and sit around Yudhishthira, who laments the death of his nephew Abhimanyu. He blames himself for sending the boy into Drona's array, and he fears Arjuna's wrath, which he expects will destroy the Kauravas. He says that even victory and sovereignty give him no joy without Abhimanyu.

scenes.B07C049S01: The Pandava warriors sit mourning, Yudhishthira blames himself for Abhimanyu's death, and predicts Arjuna's vengeance on the Kauravas.

shots.B07C049S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Pandava warriors laying down their arms and Yudhishthira lamenting Abhimanyu, blaming himself for sending him into Drona's array and predicting Arjuna's vengeance.

B07C050.summary: Yudhishthira continues to grieve, saying a child was sent into an unequal battle and he cannot find peace of mind. Vyasa comforts him, saying the heroic youth has gone to heaven and that Death takes all beings. Yudhishthira asks what Death is, and Vyasa begins the story of King Akampana, whose son Hari was slain, which Narada told the king to ease his grief.

scenes.B07C050S01: Yudhishthira laments Abhimanyu's death, Vyasa tries to console him, and Yudhishthira asks what Death is.
scenes.B07C050S02: Vyasa tells the story of King Akampana, whose son was slain, and of Narada's account of the origin of Death.

shots.B07C050S01H01: Sanjaya says the sage Vyasa comes to Yudhishthira, who laments that Abhimanyu, a child, was sent into an unequal battle and cannot regain his peace of mind.
shots.B07C050S01H02: Sanjaya says that Vyasa addresses the grieving Yudhishthira.
shots.B07C050S01H03: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that wise men are not stunned by calamity, that the youth has gone to heaven, and that Death takes all beings.
shots.B07C050S01H04: Yudhishthira asks what Death is, whose child he is, and why he takes living creatures.
shots.B07C050S01H05: Sanjaya says that Vyasa, comforting Yudhishthira, prepares to answer.
shots.B07C050S02H01: Vyasa introduces the story of King Akampana, told by Narada, which is said to ease grief and is worth hearing every morning.
shots.B07C050S02H02: Narada's account: King Akampana, whose son Hari was slain in battle, asks Narada who Death is and what his power is.
shots.B07C050S02H03: Narada begins the tale of how Brahma, finding creation without decay, let his anger create a fire that threatened to consume the universe, and how Shiva came to him.

B07C051.summary: Shiva (Sthanu) begs Brahma to be gracious, since the fire of his wrath is consuming creation. Brahma explains that the earth had asked him to destroy her burdensome creatures, and that his anger rose when he could find no other means. Shiva pleads with him to quench the fire and spare the worlds, and Brahma holds in his wrath, from which a dark woman then emerges. Brahma names her Death and orders her to slay creatures, and she weeps, and Brahma catches her tears in his hands.

scenes.B07C051S01: Shiva pleads with Brahma to stop his fire, Brahma explains his anger, Shiva asks for mercy, and Brahma names Death and sets her to her task.

shots.B07C051S01H01: Shiva (Sthanu) tells Brahma that his creatures are being consumed by his fire and asks him to be gracious.
shots.B07C051S01H02: Brahma says he wanted only the good of the earth, but his wrath rose when the earth, burdened by creatures, pressed him to destroy them and he could find no means.
shots.B07C051S01H03: Shiva (Rudra) asks Brahma to restrain his wrath, since the fire is destroying rocks, rivers, trees and every living thing.
shots.B07C051S01H04: Narada says Brahma held in his wrath, a dark woman came out of his senses, and Brahma named her Death and ordered her to kill creatures; she wept, and Brahma caught her tears in his hands.

B07C052.summary: Narada continues the tale: Death, the woman Brahma has made, pleads not to be forced into killing creatures and turns to long austerities instead. Brahma tells her to take lives anyway, promising that no sin will fall on her, and she agrees out of fear of his curse. Narada consoles King Akampana by saying death is ordained for all and that his son's fate is not a cause for grief, and Vyasa then urges Yudhishthira to cast off his own grief and go back to battle.

scenes.B07C052S01: Narada tells how Death pleads with Brahma, is told to kill anyway, performs austerities, is ordered again, and finally accepts, and how Narada comforts Akampana.
scenes.B07C052S02: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to cast off grief, recalls Abhimanyu's heavenly reward, and urges him to set out for battle.

shots.B07C052S01H01: Narada tells how Death, unwilling to take life, pleads with Brahma and asks to be allowed to practise austerities instead.
shots.B07C052S01H02: Brahma tells Death to destroy creatures, saying the task is hers and no one will blame her for it.
shots.B07C052S01H03: Narada says that Death, frightened, turned away from Brahma and spent a vast span of time in austerities at sacred places until Brahma asked her why she was so severe.
shots.B07C052S01H04: Brahma tells Death that no sin will be hers, that her tears will become diseases, and that she must take the lives of creatures.
shots.B07C052S01H05: Narada says Death, fearing Brahma's curse, agreed, and he tells Akampana that death is ordained and that he should stop grieving for his son.
shots.B07C052S02H01: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to cast off his grief, notes that Abhimanyu has won heaven by his heroism, and urges him to set out for battle with his brothers.

B07C053.summary: Yudhishthira, still grieving, asks Vyasa for more examples of royal sages and their sacrifices. Vyasa tells the story of King Srinjaya, whose son's waste and sweat turned to gold and who was killed by robbers who wanted that wealth. Narada then consoles the grieving king with the example of Marutta, a royal sage of great sacrifice who also died.

scenes.B07C053S01: Yudhishthira asks for more examples, and Vyasa tells the story of Srinjaya's gold-producing son, his death at the hands of robbers, and Narada's consolation using King Marutta.

shots.B07C053S01H01: Sanjaya says Yudhishthira humbly asks Vyasa for more words of consolation.
shots.B07C053S01H02: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa to tell him of royal sages of old, their sacrifices and their gifts, to console him.
shots.B07C053S01H03: Vyasa tells how Srinjaya's gold-producing son was slain by robbers, and how Narada consoles the grieving king with the example of Marutta, who also died.

B07C054.summary: Narada tells Srinjaya that King Suhotra, a mighty and generous ruler whose kingdom seemed to flow with gold, also met death after a life of sacrifices. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifices, since such a great king has died too.

scenes.B07C054S01: Narada recounts Suhotra's wealth, sacrifices and death, and tells Srinjaya not to grieve for a son who gave no sacrifices.

shots.B07C054S01H01: Narada recounts King Suhotra's wealth, his great sacrifices and his death, and tells Srinjaya not to mourn a son who made no sacrifices.

B07C055.summary: Narada tells Srinjaya that King Paurava, who gave away countless horses, elephants, cars and cattle at his sacrifices, also died. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who gave nothing away.

scenes.B07C055S01: Narada recounts King Paurava's vast gifts at his sacrifices and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve for his son.

shots.B07C055S01H01: Narada recounts King Paurava's great gifts at his Horse-sacrifices and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve for a son who gave nothing.

B07C056.summary: Narada tells Srinjaya that King Sivi, son of Usinara, who gave away gold, cattle and even the earth to the Brahmins, also died. Rudra had granted him a boon of inexhaustible wealth and fame, and Narada again tells Srinjaya that he should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifices.

scenes.B07C056S01: Narada recounts King Sivi's enormous gifts, Rudra's boon, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve for his son.

shots.B07C056S01H01: Narada recounts King Sivi's vast gifts, Rudra's boon, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve for a son who made no sacrifices.

B07C057.summary: Narada continues his list of dead kings, which he gives to Srinjaya to ease his grief. He describes Rama, son of Dasaratha, who lived in exile, defeated the Rakshasa Ravana who had abducted his wife, and then ruled a golden age of long life and piety. Rama too died, so Narada tells Srinjaya again not to grieve for a son who made no sacrifices.

scenes.B07C057S01: Narada recounts Rama's exile, his slaying of Ravana, his golden reign and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve for his son.

B07C058.summary: Narada recalls King Bhagiratha, who gave vast gifts at his sacrifices, with cars, cattle and maidens to the Brahmins. The river Ganga, in the story, chose him as her father by sitting on his lap, and he ascended to the realm of Brahma at the end of his life. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who gave nothing, since such a great king has died too.

scenes.B07C058S01: Narada recounts Bhagiratha's gifts, the river Ganga choosing him as her father, and his ascent to heaven, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

shots.B07C058S01H01: Narada recounts Bhagiratha's gifts and the river Ganga's sitting on his lap, and urges Srinjaya again not to grieve for his son.

B07C059.summary: Narada says that King Dilipa, son of Havila, held hundreds of sacrifices, gave the whole earth to the Brahmins, and had golden roads laid for his guests. Dilipa too died, so Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no offering.

scenes.B07C059S01: Narada recounts Dilipa's hundreds of sacrifices, his gift of the earth and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C060.summary: Narada tells of Mandhatri, son of Yuvanashva, who was brought out of his father's womb by the Ashvins and nourished from Indra's fingers, and who went on to conquer the whole earth. He performed a hundred Horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rajasuyas and gave away great treasures before dying. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who gave nothing away.

scenes.B07C060S01: Narada recounts Mandhatri's unusual birth, his conquests, his vast sacrifices and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

shots.B07C060S01H01: Narada recounts Mandhatri's unusual birth, his conquests and sacrifices, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C061.summary: Narada tells of Yayati, son of Nahusha, who performed many sacrifices and gave away the wealth of the earth. He later saw that desire is never satisfied, so he gave up his throne to his son and retired to the forest, but he too died. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifice.

scenes.B07C061S01: Narada recounts Yayati's sacrifices, his lesson that desire is never satisfied, his retreat to the forest, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C062.summary: Narada tells of Amvarisha, son of Nabhaga, who fought a thousand kings alone and defeated them, and then held a hundred splendid sacrifices with lavish feasts and gifts of kingdoms to his priests. The great sages praised him, yet he too died. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifice.

scenes.B07C062S01: Narada recounts Amvarisha's single-handed victories, his hundred sacrifices and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C063.summary: Narada says King Sasavindu had a hundred thousand wives, each of whom bore a thousand sons, all of whom performed sacrifices. At his Horse-sacrifice Sasavindu gave away his sons and enormous wealth to the Brahmins, and he too died after a long reign. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifice.

B07C064.summary: Narada tells of Gaya, son of Amartaraya, who lived on the leftovers of the sacred butter offered to Agni for a hundred years, until Agni granted him learning, wealth and sons. He then held great sacrifices, including one with a golden altar, but he too died. Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who gave no sacrifice.

scenes.B07C064S01: Narada recounts Gaya's long devotion, Agni's boons, his splendid sacrifices and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C065.summary: Narada tells of Rantideva, who kept a great host of cooks to feed Brahmins day and night, gave away gold by the crore, and sacrificed so many animals that a river was named after their hides. He too died, and Narada says Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who gave nothing away.

scenes.B07C065S01: Narada recounts Rantideva's feeding of Brahmins, his gifts of gold, the river named after his sacrificial hides, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C066.summary: Narada continues with Bharata, son of Dushyanta, who as a boy in the forest mastered lions, tigers and elephants and so earned the name Sarvadamana, meaning the subduer of all. As an adult he performed many Horse-sacrifices and gave away enormous wealth, including gold to Kanva. He too died, so Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifice.

scenes.B07C066S01: Narada recounts Bharata's childhood mastery over wild beasts, his many Horse-sacrifices and gifts, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

shots.B07C066S01H01: Narada recounts Bharata's childhood mastery over lions and elephants, his many Horse-sacrifices and gifts, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C067.summary: Narada tells of Prithu, son of Vena, crowned emperor at a Rajasuya, whose reign brought plenty: the earth yielded crops unbidden, the cows gave milk, and sea and mountains made way for him. When his subjects asked for food, he made the Earth yield her milk, with each class of beings milking her into its own vessel. He gave away golden images at his great Horse-sacrifice, and he too died, so Srinjaya should not grieve.

scenes.B07C067S01: Narada describes Prithu's golden reign, his milking of the Earth by all classes of beings, his great gifts, and his death, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

B07C068.summary: Narada tells of Rama, son of Jamadagni, who avenged his father by destroying Kartavirya and many thousands of Kshatriyas, filling lakes with their blood. After a hundred sacrifices he gave the earth to the sage Kasyapa, who told him to leave it, and he withdrew to Mount Mahendra. He too will die, Narada says, so Srinjaya should not grieve for a son who made no sacrifice.

scenes.B07C068S01: Narada recounts Rama's campaign against the Kshatriyas, his gift of the earth to Kasyapa, his retreat to Mount Mahendra, and the fact that all such great men die, and again tells Srinjaya not to grieve.

shots.B07C068S01H01: Narada recounts Rama's avenging of his father, his destruction of the Kshatriyas, his gift of the earth to Kasyapa, and his retreat, and urges Srinjaya not to grieve for his son.

B07C069.summary: Srinjaya, having heard the histories of the sixteen kings, says his grief has been dispelled and asks Narada what he should do. Narada offers him any boon, and Srinjaya asks only for Narada's favour, so Narada restores his slain son from hell. Vyasa then explains that Abhimanyu died bravely and has won heaven, and bids Yudhishthira rise and fight, before departing, leaving Yudhishthira consoled but troubled about facing Arjuna.

scenes.B07C069S01: Srinjaya's grief is lifted, Narada restores his son, Vyasa draws the lesson of Abhimanyu's death, and Yudhishthira, consoled, worries about facing Arjuna.

shots.B07C069S01H01: Vyasa reports that Srinjaya, silent after the histories, tells Narada his grief is gone and asks what he should do now.
shots.B07C069S01H02: Narada tells Srinjaya that his grief is gone and that he may ask any boon.
shots.B07C069S01H03: Srinjaya replies that it is enough that Narada is pleased with him.
shots.B07C069S01H04: Narada promises to bring back Srinjaya's son, who was slain by robbers, from the terrible hell where he went.
shots.B07C069S01H05: Vyasa describes the restored son, sets Abhimanyu's brave death above him, bids Yudhishthira rise and not grieve, departs, and leaves Yudhishthira consoled but still troubled about facing Arjuna.

B07C070.summary: At sunset Arjuna, having destroyed many Samsaptakas, rides back to camp with Krishna, uneasy at omens and at the grim silence. He finds his brothers grieving and realizes Abhimanyu is missing, and he breaks into a long lament, asking how the boy died. He also learns that Yuyutsu rebuked the Kaurava heroes for rejoicing, and Krishna consoles him that warriors fall bravely in battle, before Yudhishthira begins to speak.

scenes.B07C070S01: Arjuna and Krishna return to camp at sunset, Arjuna finds the camp joyless and his brothers grieving, Arjuna laments Abhimanyu's death, and Krishna consoles him.

shots.B07C070S01H01: Sanjaya describes the close of the day, Arjuna's return from slaying the Samsaptakas, and his fear of omens as he asks Krishna whether his brother and friends are safe.
shots.B07C070S01H02: Krishna says the king and his friends are surely well and that Arjuna should not grieve over some minor misfortune elsewhere.
shots.B07C070S01H03: Arjuna finds the camp joyless, with no music or songs, and asks Krishna whether his brothers and allies are safe.
shots.B07C070S01H04: Arjuna sees his brothers grieving, asks for Abhimanyu, and laments his son's death at length, blaming the warriors and hearing Yuyutsu's rebuke of the Kaurava heroes.
shots.B07C070S01H05: Krishna consoles Arjuna by saying that death in battle is the way of heroes, and Arjuna sits in grief until Yudhishthira begins to speak.

B07C071.summary: Yudhishthira tells Arjuna how Abhimanyu broke Drona's array, how Jayadratha's boon checked the Pandavas, and how six warriors surrounded the boy and cut him off from his car. Duhsasana's son finally killed him after he had slain thousands. Arjuna faints with grief, rises in fury, and swears to slay Jayadratha by the next sunset or enter the fire, invoking dire fates on himself if he fails. He stretches the Gandiva and blows his conch, and the Pandava camp answers with shouts.

scenes.B07C071S01: Yudhishthira recounts Abhimanyu's death, Arjuna swoons and rises in rage, swears two oaths to kill Jayadratha, and sounds his conch.

shots.B07C071S01H01: Yudhishthira recounts Abhimanyu's breaking of the array, Jayadratha's boon checking the Pandavas, the six warriors' attack, and Abhimanyu's death at the hands of Duhsasana's son, and Arjuna falls in grief.
shots.B07C071S01H02: Arjuna swears to slay Jayadratha the next day, whatever allies may protect him, and calls down the fate of sinners on himself if he fails.
shots.B07C071S01H03: Arjuna's second oath: if Jayadratha is not slain by the next sunset he will enter the fire, and even if Jayadratha hides in the underworld or heaven, he will cut off his head.

B07C072.summary: On hearing the Pandava uproar, Jayadratha is terrified by Arjuna's oath and asks Duryodhana's leave to go home. Duryodhana reassures him by naming the great warriors who will surround and protect him. That night Jayadratha asks Drona how his skill compares with Arjuna's, and Drona answers that Arjuna is the better through discipline, but promises an array Arjuna cannot pierce.

scenes.B07C072S01: Jayadratha, frightened by Arjuna's vow, asks to leave, Duryodhana reassures him, and that night Drona answers his question about Arjuna's skill and promises protection.

shots.B07C072S01H01: Jayadratha, stricken by fear of Arjuna's vow, asks leave to go home, and Duryodhana reassures him by naming the great warriors who will surround him.
shots.B07C072S01H02: That night Jayadratha goes to Drona and asks him to compare Jayadratha's own skill in archery with Arjuna's.
shots.B07C072S01H03: Drona says Arjuna is superior through discipline and hardship, promises to form an array Arjuna cannot pierce, and urges Jayadratha to act as a warrior should.

B07C073.summary: Krishna rebukes Arjuna for swearing an oath without consulting him, and he reports the spies' news that the Kauravas are dismayed. Jayadratha, shaking with fear, pleads with Duryodhana for protection, and Duryodhana turns to Drona. Drona arranges a formation half cart and half lotus, with Jayadratha at its heart and six champions guarding him.
